title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378ZL (Investment in other companies, formation of subsidiaries, etc.)

content.overview: Section 378ZL governs Producer Company investments and subsidiaries. It addresses investment of general reserves, acquisition of shares in another Producer Company, investment or arrangements with other bodies corporate to promote the company's objects, a general thirty-per-cent limit for specified other-company investments with a special-resolution and prior Central Government approval exception, consistency with the company's objects, disposal approvals, and a register of investments open to Member inspection.
content.glance: Section 378ZL sets investment powers and limits, approval conditions, object-consistency requirements and a Member-inspectable investment register.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 378ZL (Investment in other companies, formation of subsidiaries, etc.). General reserves are to be invested to secure the highest returns available from the specified approved securities, fixed deposits, units or bonds issued by Government or a co-operative or scheduled bank, or another prescribed mode. A Producer Company may acquire shares in another Producer Company to promote its objects and may subscribe to another body's share capital or enter arrangements such as a subsidiary or joint venture for that purpose by special resolution. Investments in other companies under subsection (4) are generally capped at thirty per cent of aggregate paid-up capital and free reserves, with the stated exception for a special resolution at a general meeting and prior Central Government approval. Investments must be consistent with the Producer Company's objects. The Board may dispose of investments under subsections (3) and (4) with prior Member approval by special resolution. The company must maintain the prescribed investment register at its registered office, open to Member inspection and extracts. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Investment of general reserves
sections.body: General reserves must be invested to secure the highest returns available from the approved securities, fixed deposits, units or bonds issued by Government or a co-operative or scheduled bank, or another mode as may be prescribed.

sections.heading: Investments to promote Producer Company objects
sections.body: A Producer Company may acquire shares of another Producer Company to promote its objects. It may also subscribe to the share capital of, or enter an agreement or other arrangement with, a body corporate, including through a subsidiary or joint venture, for promoting its objects by special resolution.

sections.heading: Other-company investment limit and exception
sections.body: Investments under subsection (4) in companies other than the Producer Companies or capital subscriptions addressed in subsections (2) and (3) must not exceed thirty per cent of aggregate paid-up capital and free reserves. The proviso permits investment above that limit by special resolution passed at a general meeting and with prior approval of the Central Government.

sections.heading: Consistency, disposal and register
sections.body: All investments must be consistent with the Producer Company's objects. The Board may dispose of investments under subsections (3) and (4) with prior Member approval by special resolution. The company must keep a register showing the names of companies invested in, number and value of shares, acquisition date, and manner and price of subsequent disposal. The register must be kept at the registered office and be open to Member inspection and extracts.

examples.title: Assessing an investment proposal
examples.body: Classify the investment route, check whether it promotes the Producer Company's objects, identify any special-resolution requirement, calculate the applicable thirty-per-cent limit where subsection (4) applies, and verify prior Central Government approval if the statutory exception is relied on. Check register and disposal requirements as relevant.

hypotheticals.question: A Producer Company proposes to invest in a non-Producer Company above the general limit in section 378ZL. What must be checked?
hypotheticals.analysis: Identify whether the investment falls within subsection (4), calculate the limit by reference to aggregate paid-up capital and free reserves, and verify both a special resolution passed in general meeting and prior Central Government approval before relying on the proviso. Also check that the investment is consistent with the Producer Company's objects and that the statutory register is maintained.

distinctions.title: Investment routes and approvals under section 378ZL
distinctions.left: Acquiring shares in another Producer Company to promote the company's objects under subsection (2).
distinctions.right: Other-company investments under subsection (4), which are subject to a general thirty-per-cent limit and a specified approval exception.

rows.right: Promotion of Producer Company objects, subject to subsection (4) limits
Thirty-per-cent cap unless special resolution and prior Central Government approval are obtained

misconceptions.trap: Applying the thirty-per-cent limit to every investment route without checking subsections (2) and (3).
misconceptions.correction: Identify the investment category and apply the subsection (4) limit only to the investments described there.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming a special resolution alone permits an investment above the subsection (4) limit.
misconceptions.correction: The proviso also requires prior approval of the Central Government.

misconceptions.trap: Treating investment powers as unrestricted by the Producer Company's objects or register duties.
misconceptions.correction: Section 378ZL requires consistency with the company's objects and maintenance of a Member-inspectable investment register.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does section 378zl do?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: A Producer Company may invest in, or form, another Producer Company or a body the section permits, with the approval and within the limits stated.

examTips: Do not apply the thirty-per-cent limit without classifying the investment route.
The proviso requires prior Central Government approval as well as a special resolution.
Remember the investment register and Member inspection provisions.
revisionPoints: General reserves are invested in the modes specified by subsection (1).
Subsection (4) has a general thirty-per-cent limit and a specified approval exception.
Investments must be consistent with the company's objects.
Disposal approval and register duties are also prescribed.
